docs.title: TrimSpeedXP user guide
docs.text:
TrimSpeedXP is a free X-Plane 12 plugin that makes pitch trim faster and smoother. In X-Plane, one press of the trim key moves the pitch trim by a tiny, fixed amount, so on many aircraft you hold the key or click the button over and over to trim for a new speed. Digital trim wheels, such as the one on the Honeycomb Bravo Throttle Quadrant, work the same way: every click of the wheel is one button press, and one tiny trim step.

TrimSpeedXP lets you choose how far one press moves the trim, separately for each aircraft. The trim then glides smoothly to the new position instead of jumping there.

  • One press moves the trim by an amount you set, from very fine (0.005 %) to coarse (20 % of the full trim travel).
  • Smooth glide to the new position, from instant up to 1 second.
  • Settings are saved per aircraft. Aircraft you haven't set up keep X-Plane's normal trim.
  • Assign your own keyboard keys and joystick buttons in the plugin window, or use X-Plane's own Keyboard and Joystick settings.
  • Works with digital trim wheels (such as the Honeycomb Bravo's): each click of the wheel moves the trim by the amount you set.
  • A live trim gauge shows where the trim is and how far one press goes.
  • No other add-ons needed (no FlyWithLua or scripts).

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
1. Installation: what you need, installing, updating and uninstalling.
  2. Quick start: set up your first aircraft in a minute.
  3. The window: every setting in the TrimSpeedXP window.
  4. Hotkeys and trim wheels: assigning keys, joystick buttons and digital trim wheels.
  5. Troubleshooting: common problems, the log and where your settings are stored.
  6. Questions and answers: what TrimSpeedXP does and does not do.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
1. Copy the TrimSpeedXP folder from the download into X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins.
  2. In X-Plane, open Plugins › FSD Trim Speed XP › Show / hide window.
  3. Click Create settings for this aircraft and turn the knob to set how far one press moves the trim.
  4. Assign your trim keys, buttons or trim wheel under Hotkeys, and go fly.

docs.title: Questions and answers
docs.text: User guide › Questions and answers

docs.title: Does it change aircraft I haven't set up?
docs.text: No. Aircraft without settings trim in X-Plane's normal small steps, and TrimSpeedXP does not block any joystick buttons on them.

docs.title: Will it fight my autopilot?
docs.text: No. If the autopilot or another control moves the trim while TrimSpeedXP is gliding, the glide stops, so they never fight.

docs.title: Do different liveries need their own settings?
docs.text: No. Aircraft are recognised by their file name (for example Cessna_172SP.acf), so all liveries of the same aircraft share one setting.

docs.title: Does it work with my trim wheel?
docs.text: Yes, if the wheel works as buttons, which is how digital trim wheels such as the Honeycomb Bravo's work. See Trim wheels.

docs.title: Can I use X-Plane's own keyboard and joystick settings instead?
docs.text: Yes. All actions are also X-Plane commands; see Using X-Plane's own settings instead.

docs.title: Do I lose my settings when I update?
docs.text: No. Settings are stored separately from the plugin, so just replace the plugin folder (see Updating).

docs.title: Do I need FlyWithLua or other add-ons?
docs.text: No. TrimSpeedXP works on its own.

docs.title: Hotkeys and trim wheels
docs.text:
User guide › Hotkeys and trim wheels

In the Hotkeys section of the window you choose which keys and joystick buttons trigger TrimSpeedXP. There are three actions: Trim up, Trim down and Show / hide window. Hotkeys are the same for all aircraft.

docs.title: Assigning a key or button
docs.text:
Click the field in the Keyboard or Joystick column, then press the key or joystick button you want. Press Esc to cancel. Click the small x next to a field to remove that assignment.

  • Keys you assign here take priority over X-Plane's own key assignments.
  • If a joystick button already has a command in X-Plane's joystick settings, it is shown under the field, for example X-Plane: sim/flight_controls/pitch_trim_up.

docs.title: Trim wheels (Honeycomb Bravo and similar)
docs.text:
Digital trim wheels don't send a position. Each click of the wheel is a joystick button press: one button for nose up, another for nose down. In X-Plane they show up as two ordinary buttons, so you assign them just like buttons:

  1. Click the Joystick field next to Trim up, then turn the wheel one click in the nose-up direction.
  2. Click the Joystick field next to Trim down, then turn the wheel one click nose down.
  3. Leave Block X-Plane's own assignment on these buttons ticked, so the wheel doesn't also move the trim through X-Plane's own setting.

Now every click moves the trim by your step size, and fast spins add up smoothly thanks to the glide.

Tuning a wheel: a wheel sends many clicks per turn, so it needs a smaller step than a button. Start around 0.25 % per click with a glide of about 0.1 s, then adjust until one comfortable turn of the wheel does what you expect.

docs.title: Blocking X-Plane's own assignment
docs.text: If the button you use here also has a command in X-Plane, one press would do two things. With Block X-Plane's own assignment on these buttons ticked (recommended), TrimSpeedXP blocks X-Plane's command on that button, so the button does only one thing. On aircraft without TrimSpeedXP settings, the button is not blocked and works as before.

docs.title: Using X-Plane's own settings instead
docs.text:
All three actions are also X-Plane commands. In X-Plane's Settings › Keyboard or Settings › Joystick, search for TrimSpeedXP and assign TrimSpeedXP/trim_up, TrimSpeedXP/trim_down or TrimSpeedXP/toggle_window.

Next: Troubleshooting

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: User guide › Installation

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• X-Plane 12.
  • Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) or Linux: any 64-bit system that runs X-Plane 12.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
1. Download the latest version from Releases and unzip it. Inside you'll find a folder called TrimSpeedXP and the user guide (PDF).

  2. Copy the whole TrimSpeedXP folder into the plugins folder of X-Plane: X-Plane 12 › Resources › plugins. It should end up like this:

    X-Plane 12/
  Resources/
    plugins/
      TrimSpeedXP/
        64/
          win.xpl
          mac.xpl
          lin.xpl

  3. Start X-Plane. In the top menu, open Plugins. You should see FSD Trim Speed XP there.

Mac users: macOS may block plugins downloaded from the internet. If TrimSpeedXP does not appear in the Plugins menu, or macOS says it "cannot be opened", open Terminal and run this command (adjust the path if X-Plane is somewhere else), then restart X-Plane:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/X-Plane 12/Resources/plugins/TrimSpeedXP"

docs.title: Updating
docs.text: Close X-Plane, delete the old TrimSpeedXP folder from Resources/plugins, and copy in the new one. Your settings are kept, because they are stored in a different place (see Where your settings are stored).

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
Close X-Plane and delete the TrimSpeedXP folder from Resources/plugins. To also remove your settings, delete the folder X-Plane 12/Output/preferences/TrimSpeedXP.

Next: Quick start

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
User guide › Quick start

  1. Load your aircraft and open Plugins › FSD Trim Speed XP › Show / hide window.
  2. Under This aircraft, click Create settings for this aircraft.
  3. Turn the knob to set how far one press moves the trim. Drag up or down on it, or scroll the mouse wheel over it.
  4. Under Hotkeys, click the Keyboard or Joystick field next to Trim up and press the key or button you want to use, or turn your trim wheel one click nose up. Do the same for Trim down (turn the wheel nose down).
  5. Close the window and fly. Each press now moves the trim by the amount you chose.

Where to start: new settings start at 2.5 % per press. Light aircraft such as the Cessna 172 usually feel good between 0.25 % and 2.5 %. For a trim wheel, start around 0.25 % per click (see Hotkeys and trim wheels).

Next: The window

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: User guide › Troubleshooting

docs.title: FSD Trim Speed XP is not in the Plugins menu
docs.text: Check the folder layout: the path must be Resources/plugins/TrimSpeedXP/64/ with the .xpl files inside 64. A common mistake is an extra folder level, such as plugins/TrimSpeedXP/TrimSpeedXP/64. On a Mac, also see the note under Installation.

docs.title: The trim wheel moves the trim the wrong way
docs.text: The two wheel directions are assigned the other way round. Assign them again: Trim up gets the nose-up direction.

docs.title: One press moves the trim twice, or by the wrong amount
docs.text: The same key or button probably also has a trim command in X-Plane. For joystick buttons, tick Block X-Plane's own assignment on these buttons. For keyboard keys, remove the key from X-Plane's trim commands in Settings › Keyboard.

docs.title: Nothing happens when I press my hotkey
docs.text: Check that Enable Trim Speed is ticked and that the aircraft has its own settings (see This aircraft). Use the Test buttons to check that the trim moves.

docs.title: Something else seems wrong
docs.text: Open X-Plane 12/Log.txt and search for lines that start with [TrimSpeedXP]. Please include them when you report a problem.

docs.title: Where your settings are stored
docs.text:
X-Plane 12/Output/preferences/TrimSpeedXP/settings.json

This file holds your hotkeys and the settings for every aircraft. It is not touched when you update or reinstall the plugin. Back it up if you reinstall X-Plane.

Next: Questions and answers

docs.title: The window
docs.text:
User guide › The window

You open and close the window from Plugins › FSD Trim Speed XP › Show / hide window, or with a hotkey you assign to Show / hide window. You can move it by dragging the title bar and resize it from the edges. The title bar shows the aircraft that is currently loaded.

docs.title: Enable Trim Speed
docs.text: The main on/off switch. When it is off, TrimSpeedXP does nothing at all, and your trim keys and buttons work exactly as they do in X-Plane.

docs.title: This aircraft
docs.text:
Settings for the aircraft you are flying. Every aircraft has its own.

If the aircraft has no settings yet, you'll see Create settings for this aircraft. Until you click it, this aircraft simply uses X-Plane's normal trim, so nothing changes for aircraft you haven't set up.

The knob sets how far one press moves the trim, as a percentage of the full trim travel (from full nose down to full nose up).

  • Drag up or down on the knob, or scroll the mouse wheel over it.
  • Hold Shift for fine steps.
  • The text beside it tells you, for example, "408 presses from full nose down to full nose up", which gives you a feel for the setting.

Where to start: new settings start at 2.5 % per press. Light aircraft such as the Cessna 172 usually feel good between 0.25 % and 2.5 %. Turn it up if trimming still takes too many presses, and down if one press is too much.

Glide sets how long the trim takes to reach its new position: from instant up to 1 second. A short glide (around 0.1 to 0.25 s) feels natural and smooth. Quick presses in a row add up, so tapping three times moves the trim three steps.

Trim gauge. The bar shows the current trim position live, from Nose down on the left to Nose up on the right, plus how far one press would take it in each direction.

Test: trim up / Test: trim down move the trim right away, so you can try your setting without reaching for a key.

Remove settings (use X-Plane default trim) deletes the settings for this aircraft. It goes back to X-Plane's normal trim.

docs.title: Hotkeys
docs.text: The keys and joystick buttons that trigger TrimSpeedXP. See Hotkeys and trim wheels.

docs.title: Saved aircraft
docs.text: A list of every aircraft that has its own TrimSpeedXP settings, with its step per press. Click x to remove an aircraft's settings. That aircraft then uses X-Plane's normal trim again.

docs.title: Bottom bar
docs.text:
Shows the version of TrimSpeedXP. FlySimDev opens the FlySimDev page with more plugins, and Donate lets you support development (both links are also in the Plugins menu).
